A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the “one-by-one insertion” mechanism is only a special case of the more general mechanism of “supersaturated insertion” which can be applied for any system of interconnected units.
the so-called intrinsic hystereses are not intrinsic, but are rather a consequence of the presence of a large number of interconnected units, each one undergoing a phase- or state transformation.
the so-called intrinsic hysteresity of insertion type of battery electrodes is a result of a combination of various phenomena.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the “one-by-one insertion” is not a single process, but a combination of two or more different processes that can occur at different stages of the insertion.
the one-by-one insertion/deinsertion mechanism is only one of many possible mechanisms that can occur in a system of interconnected units, and that it is not necessarily a universal mechanism.
the “one-by-one insertion mechanism” can occur even at very low insertion rates.
